parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
cant is insincere, hypocritical talk

explanation.surface: Someone wavers over whether a pious stance was just hypocrisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like part of the definition phrase but supplies RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw a statement or belief is what someone does after changing their mind.

clue.text: Killing of many people over a defined area

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: the masses are the people at large
an acre is a fixed measured area of land

explanation.surface: A report on the slaughter of a crowd within a set zone.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesale slaughter is by definition the killing of a large number.

indicators.note: being aboard a ship means being inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of the word once are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Baking done in a ship's galley in days gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges ONCE to CONE, which goes 'aboard' SS. Scones are small British baked cakes, often served with jam and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Small plain baked goods eaten at teatime are a kind of cake.

clue.text: Region that is not party to the convention

definitions.meaning: a historic area of central Europe, now part of the Czech Republic

definitions.text: that is not party to the convention
definitions.meaning: the world of artists and free spirits who live outside conventional society

explanation.surface: A territory that refuses to sign an international treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convention' reads as a treaty but means social convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The Czech province gave its name to the unconventional artistic community and lifestyle.

indicators.note: to turn something is to change its arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reporter waiting for a go on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges TO RIDE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who prepares and revises newspaper copy is a kind of journalist.

clue.text: Quartz watch that doesn't look real?

parts.note: quartz is a crystalline mineral, rock crystal, loosely glass
to eye something is to watch it

explanation.surface: A quartz timepiece that looks like a cheap fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' poses as a timepiece; the definition puns on an artificial eye that cannot see and is not real.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial eye neither sees nor is a natural organ, so it doesn't look and isn't real.

clue.text: By no fluke does this slow the boat down

definitions.text: By no fluke does this slow the boat down

parts.words: By no fluke does this slow the boat down
parts.note: a fluke is the barbed blade of an anchor; this floating drogue has none, yet still slows a vessel

explanation.surface: Insisting it's no accident that something slows the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluke' reads as a lucky chance but is the hooked part of an ordinary anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: A drogue dragged in the water steadies and slows a vessel without gripping the seabed.

clue.text: Blissful time, messing about idly on lake

indicators.note: messing something about jumbles it, so the letters of idly are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A happy spell spent pottering idly by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messing about' suggests aimless loafing but is the anagram signal working on 'idly'; L is the standard map abbreviation for lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of perfect peace and happiness, as in a pastoral poem, is an idyll.

clue.text: Person who makes no effort to move

definitions.text: Person who makes no effort to move

parts.words: Person who makes no effort to move
parts.note: a traveller carried along in a vehicle without doing any of the work, also a team member who shirks

explanation.surface: A complaint about a lazy colleague who won't budge.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a slacker; it is also someone carried on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider in a car or train travels without driving, and a shirker coasts on others' work.

clue.text: Good man has criminal to hide away

parts.note: ST, saint, is the crossword shorthand for a good man

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters of has are rearranged

explanation.surface: A virtuous man has a crook for whom he must hide something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a noun but rearranges HAS to ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: To store something secretly is to squirrel it away.

clue.text: A force raised at some distance

indicators.note: in a down entry a raised word is read from bottom to top, so it runs backwards

parts.note: RAF is the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: An air force takes off at a distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns RAF to FAR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seen from a long way off is seen from far away.

definitions.meaning: flowering plants, things that bloom; scented garden flowers
a stock was a stiff cloth band worn round the neck in earlier centuries

explanation.surface: Ladies' baggy knickers are dated clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' reads as baggy underwear but means flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a cottage-garden flower and a period neckcloth.

parts.note: being in means being at home
former means earlier or previous

explanation.surface: Lawn spotted at a house before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' poses as lawn; in slang it means someone who tells on criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is a police informant.

clue.text: One thousand troops heading southeast in huge formation

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
the Roman numeral for a thousand
soldiers are men
SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast

explanation.surface: A thousand soldiers march southeast in a vast column.
explanation.walkthrough: I and M are Roman numerals; 'heading', 'in' and 'formation' only dress the military picture and give no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vast or enormous in size is immense.

definitions.meaning: a sailing warship that bore a crew of seamen

explanation.surface: A soldier transporting naval men.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase names a warrior and an old armed ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a warrior and a historic sailing warship.

clue.text: Bird that is cut up and smoked

definitions.meaning: a seabird related to the cormorant

definitions.text: that is cut up and smoked

explanation.surface: A bird that gets butchered and smoked like fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture misleads: the second sense is tobacco, not meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a crested seabird and finely shredded pipe tobacco.

definitions.meaning: a fishing boat that uses drift nets
a person who wanders aimlessly without a home

explanation.surface: A vessel which may be a tramp steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' also suggests a tramp ship, but here it is a vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a drift-net fishing boat and an aimless wanderer.

parts.note: a route or way meant for pedestrians, people going on foot rather than by car

explanation.surface: Lessons for people who have never learnt to drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests lessons, or a golf course for non-golfers; it is a path.
explanation.definitionFit: A track for walkers is a route used by people not in vehicles.

indicators.note: something spread about has its parts scattered, so the letters of disease are rearranged

explanation.surface: An infection that may be carried by water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly spread' rearranges DISEASE; 'by water' looks like the means of transmission but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast is the place beside the sea.

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batsman is safe when in his crease, the marked line at the wicket

explanation.surface: A great spot for a cricketer at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like an adjective meaning great, but it is a verb. The crease is the line in cricket behind which the batsman stands.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow larger is to increase, and a batsman behind the line is in the crease.

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of hordes are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild hordes running riot round the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' rearranges HORDES; the definition describes a place found in that sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek island lies in the eastern Mediterranean.

parts.note: split Abeam into a beam; a beam is a plank or board, and being on a ship is being on board

explanation.surface: Asking whether abeam is a nautical position on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abeam' is a real sailing term, at right angles to the keel, but it must be split as a word play on a beam, a timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on or in a vessel is the everyday sense; 'a beam' gives 'a board'.

definitions.meaning: the means or action by which something is done
a firm providing a service, such as an advertising or travel firm

explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers instrumentality, as in 'through the agency of', and a service company.

indicators.note: out signals the letters of in rota are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Dividing out tasks according to a rota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Share out' reads as one verb, but 'out' rearranges IN ROTA and 'Share' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed allowance, as in wartime food, is a portion or share.

definitions.meaning: astir or in progress, as a plan that is under way
twelve inches make one foot of length

explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'approximately' but means astir, in progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going on or in progress, such as a plan, is said to be under way.

clue.text: Treatment for a stoop? The appropriate specialist here

indicators.note: treating something works it over, so the letters of a stoop and the are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on curing a hunched back, recommending a suitable expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treatment for' rearranges A STOOP THE; the surface is a medical recommendation that the answer fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner who manipulates bones and joints is the right expert for a bad posture.

parts.note: the biblical city where the building of a great tower ended in a confusion of tongues

explanation.surface: Where a furious argument broke out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towering row' reads as a huge argument, but it is a noisy confusion at a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the tower-building city became a byword for noisy confusion of languages.

clue.text: Improvement of action due to training

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters of action due are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting better performance thanks to practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' rearranges ACTION DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling develops and improves the mind.
